headline: SpaceXAI, Elon Musk's AI company, testified before a New York City Council committee only after a subpoena and was sharply questioned about the safety of its Grok chatbot.
score_reason: Pool 6 kept: a follow-up with new testimony and a public clash, but a city hearing with no finding or rule.
importance_line: New Yorkers who use or are targeted by AI chatbots, and the lawmakers drafting 10 AI bills, got an early public test of how a major AI company answers local oversight, but a hearing is not a ruling and SpaceXAI's representative said she could not speak to the specific case.
summary: The New York Daily News reports that Gabriela Castillo Madrid, SpaceXAI's senior manager of global government affairs, testified at the City Council's Technology Committee hearing on 16 Oct 2026 after the company was compelled by a subpoena, which we noted in our 14 Oct 2026 edition when CNBC reported that it had agreed to appear. Council Speaker Julie Menin challenged her over safety controls on Grok, SpaceXAI's chatbot, saying she found a sexualized image of herself made with it within seconds, and Castillo Madrid said she could not speak to that case and that Grok has "strict controls"; the Council is weighing 10 bills to regulate the AI industry.
notes: The pool source, Spectrum News NY1, has only a short teaser (it also says the company skipped the previous week's hearing and testified only after a subpoena), so the details come from the New York Daily News and it is credited. CNBC and Quartz not opened (403). Crain's New York headline says 'under 30 seconds' while Menin is quoted as saying 'within a second', so the entry says 'within seconds'. Follow-up of the 14 Oct 2026 edition item 'SpaceX agrees to testify to NYC Council about AI safety after receiving subpoena' (CNBC).
